core_reliability_principles.problem_addressed: Ambiguous code forces maintainers to infer meaning from implementation details.
core_reliability_principles.context: A public API or shared module needs to communicate how it should be used.
recommended_approach: Prefer constructs whose normal Python meaning matches the intended operation.
Choose names, collection operations, and control flow that make the expected use obvious.
invalid_states_prevented: A caller mistakes a sequence for a mapping or a one-shot iterator for reusable data.
runtime_failures_prevented: Maintenance bugs from surprising iteration, mutation, or ordering behavior.
type_checker_implications: Makes at least part of the contract visible to static analysis when the chosen type checker supports the feature.
Does not replace runtime validation at I/O, user, network, database, or configuration boundaries.
testability_implications: Creates a narrower surface for unit tests by making valid and invalid cases explicit.
Boundary tests should still exercise malformed runtime data and tool gaps.
maintenance_implications: Documents intent in executable signatures and data shapes instead of relying only on comments.
May require migration work where existing callers rely on looser or ambiguous values.
tradeoffs: Intent-revealing code can be slightly more verbose than clever compact code.
use_when: A public API or shared module needs to communicate how it should be used.
do_not_use_when: A local expression is genuinely obvious and extra wrapping would obscure the algorithm.
common_misuses: Using unusual collection types only to appear clever.
review_questions: Can a caller construct or pass an invalid value despite this design?
